cohort: Births in the US from 2003 to 2011, comparing 9,587 births among women with bariatric surgery to 221,580 births among morbidly obese women
finding: Women who underwent bariatric surgery had overall improved pregnancy outcomes compared to morbidly obese women, but were more likely to experience venous thromboembolisms, require blood transfusions, have induced labor, and experience fetal growth restriction.
mod_finding: Women with bariatric surgery had lower rates of cesarean delivery and instrumental delivery compared to morbidly obese women.
